channel.title: Papers on Yichen(Andy) Yu
channel.description: Recent content in Papers on Yichen(Andy) Yu

item.title: GenLARP: Enabling Immersive Live Action Role Play through LLM-Generated Worlds and Characters
item.description: ISMAR 2025 Poster: GenLARP leverages large language models to generate interactive worlds and AI-driven characters, enabling immersive live action role play (LARP) for collaborative learning and narrative exploration.

item.title: NieNie: Adaptive Rhythmic System for Stress Relief with LLM-Based Guidance
item.description: ISWC 2025: NieNie, an adaptive rhythmic system combining stress detection, biofeedback, and LLM-based guidance through interactive squeezing gameplay.

item.title: Noetic Dream: A Personalized VR and Meditation System for Lucid Dream Training
item.description: UIST Adjunct ’25: Noetic Dream integrates personalized VR dream reconstruction, anomaly-detection gameplay, and open-monitoring (OM) meditation to train lucid dreaming.

item.title: RunPacer: A Smartwatch-Based Vibrotactile Feedback System for Symmetric Co-Running by Visually Impaired Individuals and Guides
item.description: ASSETS 2025 poster: RunPacer, a smartwatch-based vibrotactile feedback system that synchronizes cadence between visually impaired runners and guides to enhance safety, autonomy, and shared agency.

item.title: Design AI for My Community: A Case Study of Collaborative Learning in a Freedom-to-Read Summer Camp
item.description: Case study of a summer camp—‘Protect the Freedom to READ’—that engaged middle school students in co-designing AI for their community, transferring AI literacy into higher-order skills through critical pedagogy and embodied tools (BeeTrap, Briteller).

item.title: Chameleon: Unobtrusive Substitution of Real-World Obstacles in VR
item.description: Chameleon is a risk-level–aware system that unobtrusively substitutes real-world obstacles inside VR, preserving immersion while improving safety and accessibility. Accepted to CHI EA 2025.

item.title: Structural Heart Abnormalities Are Prevalent on the 12-Lead Electrocardiogram Among Firefighters
item.description: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine (Aug 2025): Routine 12-lead ECG screening among firefighters revealed prevalent conduction abnormalities and coronary indicators (2011–2019).
